coordinates.note: The official ANTARES site states only "a latitude of 43° North"; the collaboration's own 2025 detector paper (arXiv:2504.09473) states the depth (2475 m) and offshore distance (40 km from Toulon) but gives no explicit degrees anywhere in the text (checked for every degree symbol and N/E pattern). Independent corroboration (re-fetched and re-checked personally by the astro-neutrino lead, not just the child that researched ANTARES): the KM3NeT Letter of Intent (arXiv:1601.07459, rank 4 design_report, sourced independently by the sibling KM3NeT child and re-verified here) states ORCA sits at 42°48'N 06°02'E, "approximately 10 kilometers west of the existing ANTARES telescope site" -- since west means lower longitude, ANTARES should be at roughly 06°02'E + ~10 km east ≈ 06°10'E at the same latitude, which matches the widely cited 42°48'N 6°10'E value (42.8°N 6.17°E) almost exactly (0.137° ≈ 11.4 km at this latitude). This upgrades confidence from 'uncertain' to 'approximate': the number is now corroborated by a rank<=7 source's relative-position statement, even though no single source states ANTARES's own degrees directly.
coordinates.quote: At about 40 km off the coast of Toulon (France), anchored at 2475 m deep in the Mediterranean Sea, there is ANTARES. / [KM3NeT LoI, on ORCA:] 42° 48' N 06° 02' E at a depth of 2450 m ... approximately 10 kilometers west of the existing ANTARES telescope site.

depth.quote: anchored at 2475 m deep in the Mediterranean Sea

name: ANTARES site (Mediterranean Sea, off Toulon)
notes: facility_id is null: no distinct facility record (e.g. a specific operating institute building) was created for ANTARES in this wave; the onshore control building was at the Institut Michel Pacha, La Seyne-sur-Mer, per the two-decades paper, but this is not modelled as a separate facility here.

summary.plain: A patch of seabed in the Mediterranean Sea, about 40 kilometres off the coast of Toulon, France, nearly 2.5 kilometres below the surface. Here the ANTARES neutrino telescope hung its cables of light sensors from 2006 until it was switched off in 2022.
summary.technical: Deep-sea site 40 km offshore from Toulon, France, at 2475 m depth in the Mediterranean Sea, hosting the ANTARES 12-line neutrino telescope from first-line deployment (2006) to shutdown (2022).
